release-artifact-tooling.title: Implement deterministic release artifact packaging
release-artifact-tooling.description: Fixture-backed deterministic system-release-tooling delivery. The node owns versioned positive and adversarial evidence under tests/release-tooling/**. Its package_component compatibility source of truth is the checked-in structured fixture tests/release-tooling/fixtures/package-component-cli-contract.json: every positive invocation is explicitly enumerated, provenance-bound to that owned file, normalized and digest-reported from its concrete structured fields, then parsed and executed through package_component.py; aggregate counters, arbitrary fixed corpus cardinalities or hashes, and synthesized placeholder command names are not evidence. The node preserves the supported reviewed-revision, Git-blob, clean-tree, and tree/blob-identity behaviors covered by those concrete invocations and rejects malformed or unsupported legacy forms for their actual parser/validation reason. Artifact Storage verification continues to use explicit signed deterministic fixtures with binding, credential-reference, compatibility/connectivity/readiness, release-manifest, and installation-index commitments, and missing or tampered evidence fails closed. Static ownership assertions for downstream release assembly and migration roots remain, but production CRDs, workloads, migrations, installers, trusted release artifacts, system-release assembly payload/consumer closure, platform release evidence, and live services remain owned and verified by downstream nodes; this node's fixtures are never production release evidence.

contract.objective: Deliver dedicated system-release-tooling primitives that package exact reviewed Git content, validate concrete package_component invocations through the real parser and execution path, bind OCI and Kubernetes fixture payloads to component identities, implement fixture-backed Compact/External Artifact Storage verification, and fail closed on dirty source, fabricated CLI evidence, fake workload provenance, invalid fixture closure, or Software Delivery ownership collisions without requiring downstream production assembly payloads.
non_goals: Do not rebuild or mutate upstream component behavior, package mutable working-tree bytes, or represent deterministic tests/release-tooling fixtures as production system-release evidence.

Do not accept mutable tags, missing digests, undeclared inputs, unindexed fixture payloads, arbitrary nested image keys, source outside declared owners, mismatched component identities, aggregate-only CLI evidence, synthesized placeholder invocations, or unsupported legacy syntax.

Do not classify OAC system-release tooling as the Software Delivery release-preview component, and do not require production CRDs, workloads, migrations, installers, trusted-release outputs, packaging/system-release payloads, owner component manifests, or completed release-assembly consumer closure in this foundational node.

contract.objective: Publish AuditEvent export/query and UsageRecord/query contracts whose detail authority comes only from a verified store event, whose CSV/JSONL export bytes are canonically derived from and exactly bound to the ordered validated redacted events and requested format, whose target CAS compares the committed revision, whose AuditEvent and UsageRecord pages preserve stable filter/order/cursor linkage, whose zero/unknown analytics fail closed, and whose nested omissions are uniquely bound to their outer field name. Deliver the canonical schema transition with only indispensable direct typed-consumer migrations in the same buildable PR; unrelated Runtime/planning repairs must already be merged by their owners.
non_goals: Do not expose a public constructor that lets a caller self-sign an AuditEvent detail binding or substitute a structurally valid caller-selected event for a store-verified immutable record.

Do not give callers authority over serialized AuditExportStream bytes; payload bytes must be canonical for the selected CSV or JSONL format, preserve validated event count and order, and contain only the explicit redacted export field matrix.

Do not accept a stream whose format differs from the ExportAuditEvents request format, or validate payload bytes independently from the event sequence, filters, scope, target, row limits, and byte limits they represent.

Do not place any field outside the explicit redacted wire matrix into AuditEvent detail, export, probe, or browser DTOs; canonical authority hashing and serialization must use the same normalized representation.
Do not treat presence of expected_revision as CAS success; update, enable, disable, and replace validation must compare it with the loaded committed target revision.
Do not accept an observed zero as known without explicit coverage evidence; omit the metric or mark it unknown with a reason, and never include unknown values in ordered rankings.
Do not accept duplicate nested omission entries or an omission whose Field differs from its outer field Name.
Do not create a second audit authority, Usage aggregate, dashboard state machine, external-SIEM fallback, or default OpenTelemetry dependency.
Do not change adjacent domain ownership or introduce a competing source of truth.
Do not bypass authorization, admission, CAS, idempotency, review or evidence gates.
Do not preserve unpublished prototype behavior unless the owning design explicitly requires it.

Do not keep Runtime SDK or internal/softwaredelivery/artifacts changes in the Audit PR. Rebase onto the two merged compensating prerequisites and remove their obsolete hunks; a worker switch alone cannot repair the current main build.

The only cross-owner supporting implementation edits permitted here are canonical AuditEvent/EvaluatedControl field/type migration and exact trusted-context/control-provenance binding in internal/agents/definitions/definitions.go and internal/softwaredelivery/preview/decision_writer.go and decision_store.go, plus their existing application_test.go, acceptance_test.go and decision_writer_test.go fixtures/regressions. Scope paths stay Audit/Usage primary ownership; these are an explicit atomic consumer exception, not new ownership. No publication/lifecycle, Preview subject, CAS/idempotency, persistence format migration or unrelated behavior redesign is authorized.

Governance reference and design documentation may synchronize the reviewed canonical contract; docs/design/detailed/10-web-api-cli-detailed-design.md may only synchronize Audit DTO terminology. No independent API/UI/product change is authorized by existing PR contents.

Do not defer compile-required direct consumer changes behind the Audit merge or add compatibility aliases, secondary audit authorities or copied production validators to avoid the transition. The existing agent-definition-audit-consumer-adaptation node remains separate owner conformance, not a second schema migration.

Implement TestAuditStoreCapabilityNilReceiptFailsClosed (new required test) for zero-valued capability, nil receipt constructor and typed-nil capability paths: return a closed authority error without panic. Retain real store-issued positive and caller-selected receipt rejection evidence; do not manufacture a passing metric.

Any new genuine prerequisite discovered by full-repository validation is an explicit owner-decision blocker, not permission to widen this exception, skip tests, reset counters, or claim a green repository.

model-catalog.title: Implement model provider catalog and discovery
model-catalog.description: Authoring recovery for the existing model-catalog delivery: consume the canonical RequestContext, authorization/admission, AuditEvent, and Credential contracts; remove production bypasses and every duplicate manual model/snapshot/digest path from core; and close the rejected concurrency, recovery, provenance, and fail-closed transport boundaries without changing adjacent owners or requiring an unmaterialized upstream artifact.

contract.objective: Deliver the governed Model Catalog boundary for provider connections, discovery snapshots, snapshot-scoped probes, and exact selection: require authenticated RequestContext, scope, authorization/admission, canonical audit evidence, and mandatory scope-bound egress before credential use; atomically bind mutations to canonical audit/outbox facts, durably finalize attempted probes, reject stale publication by connection revision/digest and predecessor CAS, and contain no manual model definition, AddManualModel, manual snapshot, or manual digest authority; the immutable model-manual owner remains separate and api-model composes both owners downstream.
non_goals: Do not modify internal/modelcatalog/manual/**, migrate model-manual ownership, consume or regenerate a model-manual component manifest, or define Model, Snapshot, AddManualModel, manual merge, or manual content digest behavior inside model-catalog. Do not create a conformance-artifact handoff when the authoritative removal option eliminates that input; any supplied model-manual artifact is outside the explicit `consumes: []` boundary and must fail closed.

Do not move RequestContext, authorization, admission, canonical AuditEvent, CredentialBroker, or durable outbox ownership into model-catalog, and do not introduce feature-local replacements for those platform facts.

Do not retain exported ungoverned production constructors, fallback actor/scope paths, origin-only default egress, credential materialization before policy approval, or public concrete store writers that bypass the governed application protocol.

Do not persist caller-controlled raw strings as non-secret headers, place Secret material in connection state or digests, leak credentials or raw provider errors, or weaken fail-closed classification at the HTTP adapter.

Do not publish a snapshot without atomic current-connection revision/configuration-digest and predecessor checks, key probe evidence without ModelCatalogSnapshotID, or leave an attempted provider call as an unrecoverable in-progress claim.

Do not add a generic provider/plugin runtime, make an external provider the source of truth, change northbound API/UI ownership, or broaden source ownership beyond internal/modelcatalog/core/** and internal/modelcatalog/providers/** plus exact tests and generated evidence.

contract.objective:
Deliver the complete protocol-neutral public harness.oac.dev/v1 SDK boundary with typed Describe, execute, observe, cancel, result, and error unions; preserve exact Package/entrypoint, Extension/binding, operation, owner, subject, scope, request digest, and service payload digest through every public binding path. Remove every public authority constructor that lets a caller choose both Host signing and trust verification inputs, and expose only the package-neutral consumer/verification side of opaque service and Gate handoffs. The SDK must define a usable Host-facing ingress contract without implementing the Host producer: arbitrary callers and ExtensionPackages must be unable to mint an authoritative RequestScope, GateEvaluatorBinding, receipt, or evaluator invocation. Replace the obsolete missing-symbol regression with a structurally valid attempt against the current public API and prove zero binding, receipt, and evaluator calls. Remove all SDK-owned or same-package test-only Host authority bridges. Every SDK-local fixture must emit source-revision-bound measured evidence for its exact scoped assertion; the Gate consumer row may pass only by proving the negative boundary, must report registered_gate_positive_path_count=0 and authoritative_gate_positive_claim_count=0, and must identify its scope as sdk-boundary rather than representing full Host-backed Gate conformance. Produce harness-sdk-boundary-evidence for the downstream harness-host producer. Preserve typed operation-schema validation, successful Trigger/EventHandler, bounded offline schema resolution, Required/Optional behavior, Unknown recovery, safe retry/cancel, coverage, race, vet, and deterministic sdk/harness packaging. The mandatory genuine Host-installed positive path and final combined semantic verdict remain downstream responsibilities of harness-host and contracts-extension. SDK-local positive operation conformance is not Host authorization: the fixed SDK conformance runner may execute ordinary typed Describe/Guide/Sensor/Executor/Trigger/EventHandler implementations with deterministic, non-authoritative request data and the same production input/response/schema/outcome validation and receipt-classification code. Its measured conformance records must be explicitly scoped sdk-operation-conformance, must not construct trusted RequestScope, service/Gate handoffs or authoritative receipts, and must never be usable by production authority entry points. A helper-only predicate or direct implementation call that bypasses the shared validation/measurement path is insufficient. Preserve successful Trigger output and all three successful EventHandler lifecycle operations; error-only implementations must fail these positive fixtures. Production typed Guide/Sensor/Trigger/EventHandler paths must finish response and output-schema validation before accepting a receipt; invalid results yield rejected/failed measured outcomes, while valid business-error envelopes retain a separate failed business outcome and never count as positive operation success. Optional side-effecting failures may become skipped only when the external failure outcome is known; structured Unknown and unstructured errors remain Unknown and require observation/recovery. SDK service/Gate rows are exclusively sdk-consumer-negative: reject even internally consistent caller handoffs without issuing a binding, authoritative receipt, or implementation/evaluator call. Envelope, rotation, replay, payload and identity assertions in these rows prove rejection of untrusted candidates, not authentication or durable replay enforcement. The Host-facing ingress contract must be package-neutral and implementable by the separately owned harness-host producer, not an unconditional rejecting stub or a caller-selectable verifier; document the exact release/entrypoint, binding, operation, owner, subject, scope, request/service-payload digest, component/run, policy and evaluator identity handoff. Host-owned verification, configured trust, expiry/rotation and replay enforcement remain in harness-host. The existing downstream dependency harness-host consumes harness-sdk-boundary-evidence and produces harness-host-gate-evidence at artifacts/harness-host/gate-evidence.json; contracts-extension consumes both and emits contracts-extension-final-conformance. Genuine service/Gate acceptance, authenticated handoff transport, accepted-then-replayed rejection across receivers/restart and genuine key rotation are mandatory Host conformance within that artifact, not SDK-local metrics or SDK prerequisites. Mark those downstream obligations not-run in SDK evidence, never passed, and do not add a reverse dependency. This clarification governs all existing test names, counters and historical decision references; no ordinary operation, schema, full identity, provenance, receipt, recovery or replay obligation is removed. The three newly required regression test names are authoring deliverables, not claims of existing passing tests: TestHarnessSDKTypedResponseValidationPrecedesReceiptAcceptance measures malformed response and output-schema violation for both Guide points, both Sensor points, Trigger, and EventHandler execute/observe/cancel (16 rejected results), plus a valid business-error envelope for each of those eight paths without false business success. TestHarnessSDKOptionalUnknownFailureRequiresObservation measures structured outcome_known=false and unstructured errors, retains Unknown without skipped Observation or retry permission, and preserves Required blocking/known Optional failure observations. TestHarnessSDKConformanceEvidenceCannotAuthorizeHostIngress submits actual fixed-runner measurements/request data to the current production service/Gate boundary and proves no authority, bindings, authoritative receipts or implementation/evaluator calls. Keep these child executions in the existing typed-point-describe-contracts, required-optional-failure-policy and service/Gate consumer rows; the fixed selector still has exactly 13 measured semantic rows and seven current-amendment rows. No new row may be faked from test-name presence. Ordinary operation rows carry actual implementation call/result and validator/receipt-classification evidence with full target/operation/provenance identity; service cases are the 15 fixed case IDs checked by the gate. All exact counters derive from those actual parent/child executions, and forbidden-call counters count only calls forbidden for that assertion, not legitimate calls in ordinary positive fixtures. Staged coverage policy, effective only after explicit human acceptance of this amendment: SDK-only raw unfiltered statement coverage must be at least 85%; this does not waive the whole-SDK 90% gate now required of downstream harness-host. Do not filter profiles, change coverage scope, pad the denominator, delete required behavior, manufacture Host proof, or move production code between owners to meet a percentage. The current 79.5% source is not accepted. Add real coverage of ordinary production-used paths and execute the exact reordered commands: broad coverage/vet/race runs first, reset the conformance log, execute every fixed boundary selector, then generate and validate the final 50-test/13-row semantic evidence once. Keep genuine Host conformance not-run in SDK evidence. An ordinary intermediate test, semantic-evidence or raw-coverage failure is implementation feedback, not by itself a terminal blocker: retain the source-bound result, diagnose the specific failing assertion or uncovered production-used path, make a substantive in-contract implementation/test correction, and measure again. Do not submit failing work as successful or advance review/merge/downstream acceptance without every unchanged gate passing. Do not repeat identical attempts without a changed source/test, a distinct evidence-backed diagnostic hypothesis, or a verified infrastructure recovery; existing bounded infrastructure retries, convergence protections and authorized budgets still apply. Request terminal blocking only with specific source-bound evidence that further lawful in-contract work cannot proceed, such as a contract/responsibility/dependency contradiction, missing authorization, indispensable external input, or an independently applicable exhausted control budget. Identify the exact source revision and contract field, actual command/result and retained evidence, attempted substantive corrections, why the next required action is unavailable within the contract, and the precise owner decision or input needed; a below-threshold percentage, one failed attempt or uncertainty about feasibility is insufficient. Use the current work-show-bound blocker protocol for a genuine blocker, never fabricate success or authority. This policy supersedes only the automatic quality-failure stopping interpretation in earlier repair reports, coordinator comments and historical stop clauses; it does not supersede security/design stop conditions or authorize a new architecture, quality relaxation, unlimited retries or a budget reset. After corrections, complete the unchanged source-bound final verification sequence in its existing order, including coverage, vet, race, all fixed selectors, semantic evidence and packaging; diagnostic runs are not final passing evidence.

Proposed recursive receipt redesign, effective only after independent review and explicit user acceptance:
Concrete candidate: one immutable measurement-tree implementation, distinct authority seals

Decision proposed, not implementation approval
Replace the proof-coupled recursive receipt representation with one internal, immutable, non-authoritative measurement tree used by BOTH the fixed SDK operation-conformance runner and authoritative ExecutionReceipt adapters. Keep authority issuance, scope validation, service verification and Gate binding exactly where they are. This is a representation/algorithm change inside sdk/harness, not a new Host issuer, new public runner, source relocation, relaxed coverage policy, or permission to accept a conformance measurement as a receipt. Only after independent review and explicit user acceptance may the existing Workers implement it.

Before / source-bound defect
At PR73 HEAD 621ba1f7a2a45c9cf6072a3cc0c25cb27c727fb8 (audit source be131f99b6cba9df1168dd0b9451c8d271e2e959), executionReceiptMeasurement.validate/digest already share leaf data checks. However ExecutionReceipt.validateWithParent, WithChildren, rebindExecutionReceiptParent and cloneExecutionReceipt traverse a recursive graph whose bookkeeping is stored in executionReceiptProof. The conformance evidence adapter in semantic_measurements_test.go:91-108 constructs proofless ExecutionReceipt-shaped trees and hashes them, but cannot exercise the production immutable child attachment, recursive relinking, comparison and defensive-copy path. It is only sharing leaf validation/hash, not the complete production representation. Repeating the leaf extraction, malformed request test, Description number test, binding-release or non-executor permission trials does not implement this proposal.

After / implementable internal structure
1. Keep executionReceiptMeasurement as the complete leaf value (including exact Package/entrypoint, Extension/binding/config, operation, owner, subject, RequestContext/ComponentRun, request/service payload digests, policy/evaluator data, accepted/rejected outcome, call count, provenance and source). Introduce one unexported measurement-tree value containing a deep-copied leaf, ordered child values and the existing parent-link digest. It carries NO RequestScope proof, SDK-issued bit, Host token, signer, verifier, callback, capability, retry permission or authority-level enum. Internal names are implementation choices, not claims of existing symbols. No public data-to-authority constructor is added.
2. Put recursive data validation, canonical parent/node/ordered-child hashing, defensive copying, attachment, recursive descendant relinking and projection-versus-snapshot comparison in this single non-authoritative engine in sdk/harness. Construction validates leaf data and each child, copies mutable slices/entrypoint values, preserves ordered children and rejects a previously bound child attached to a different parent identity. Parent identity is computed from the existing canonical leaf and its own parent linkage, excluding child digests; node identity includes ordered child digests. Preserve the current canonical serialization and nil/empty normalization so existing valid receipt digests do not silently change. Root and nested linkage, duplicate/reordered/removed children, and altered leaf data must be observable. No new persistent record or universal tree framework is needed.
3. Retain ExecutionReceipt and all current exported fields, JSON tags and methods. The private executionReceiptProof becomes an authority seal over an immutable measurement-tree snapshot instead of duplicating the recursive data algorithm. Do not retain NewHostScopeIssuer/NewHostTrustStore-style public authority composition that treats a caller-selected signer, key resolver, replay guard, provider, callable, literal marker, or same-package test fixture as Host provenance.
Do not construct a Host service or Gate handoff through sdk/harness/internal or a test-only bridge, and do not claim a negative-only SDK row as the real registered Host positive path.
Do not expose a standalone caller-supplied Gate evaluator, accept extension-created handoffs, or treat repeated equal return values as sufficient purity or Host-origin evidence.

Do not add a caller-supplied secret or key-material path, or expose attestation material without exact Package/entrypoint, Extension/binding, operation, owner, subject, scope, request digest, service payload digest, expiry, rotation, and replay binding.

Do not create a second executor, lifecycle controller, persistence store, generic plugin runtime, universal invoke(any) path, authorization or admission engine, Package authority, state-write path, or Gate bypass.

Do not let an ExtensionPackage omit, select, replace, weaken, or self-report mandatory SDK boundary fixtures; test-name presence, compile failure against a removed symbol, expected counters, helper-only predicates, or literal status values are not evidence.

Do not resolve Describe-provided schemas through arbitrary file or network references, perform host-side I/O during schema validation, accept unbounded schema/payload size or depth, or convert an unknown external outcome into failure or retry permission.

Do not change adjacent domain ownership, redefine contracts-extension-wire, move Harness decisions into Package Governance, Workflow, or a delivery adapter, or bypass Authorization, Execution Admission, CAS, idempotency, review, or evidence gates.

Do not authorize production binding from a conformance record or fixture request; do not introduce a fixture-mode switch, SDK-owned issuer, same-package private-field injection, caller-selected verifier or internal test bridge into the service/Gate authority path. Public fixed conformance runners measure ordinary extension behavior only and cannot grant Host provenance.

Do not call untrusted first-attempt/repeated rejection proof of a functioning authenticated replay store or key rotation; do not count fixture success as a Host positive path. Full Host-installed positive and replay/rotation conformance remains mandatory downstream, and absent downstream evidence is not-run, not pass.

Do not accept invalid typed response/output schema in a receipt, treat a valid business-error envelope as positive business success, or skip an Optional side-effecting failure whose external outcome is unknown.

Do not treat an immutable measurement-tree value, its digest or successful data validation as an authority seal. Every receipt node must retain production-only authority proof; conformance cannot mint it. Do not change public receipt signatures, JSON tags or canonical digest bytes, Host ingress, original fixed selector metrics, or any of the three raw coverage gates.

Do not repeat the exhausted two-increment narrow handoff or unchanged evidence-only turns: continue substantive implementation and testing of the already approved shared recursive representation under the intermediate-failure policy; a failed quality check alone is not a terminal blocker. No source relocation, removal of required validation, denominator padding or measurement-only production branch.

integration_gates.name: harness-sdk-gate
integration_gates.delivery_goal: Deliver the complete protocol-neutral public harness.oac.dev/v1 SDK boundary with typed Describe, execute, observe, cancel, result, and error unions; preserve exact Package/entrypoint, Extension/binding, operation, owner, subject, scope, request digest, and service payload digest through every public binding path. Remove every public authority constructor that lets a caller choose both Host signing and trust verification inputs, and expose only the package-neutral consumer/verification side of opaque service and Gate handoffs. The SDK must define a usable Host-facing ingress contract without implementing the Host producer: arbitrary callers and ExtensionPackages must be unable to mint an authoritative RequestScope, GateEvaluatorBinding, receipt, or evaluator invocation. Replace the obsolete missing-symbol regression with a structurally valid attempt against the current public API and prove zero binding, receipt, and evaluator calls. Remove all SDK-owned or same-package test-only Host authority bridges. Every SDK-local fixture must emit source-revision-bound measured evidence for its exact scoped assertion; the Gate consumer row may pass only by proving the negative boundary, must report registered_gate_positive_path_count=0 and authoritative_gate_positive_claim_count=0, and must identify its scope as sdk-boundary rather than representing full Host-backed Gate conformance. Produce harness-sdk-boundary-evidence for the downstream harness-host producer. Preserve typed operation-schema validation, successful Trigger/EventHandler, bounded offline schema resolution, Required/Optional behavior, Unknown recovery, safe retry/cancel, coverage, race, vet, and deterministic sdk/harness packaging. The mandatory genuine Host-installed positive path and final combined semantic verdict remain downstream responsibilities of harness-host and contracts-extension. SDK-local positive operation conformance is not Host authorization: the fixed SDK conformance runner may execute ordinary typed Describe/Guide/Sensor/Executor/Trigger/EventHandler implementations with deterministic, non-authoritative request data and the same production input/response/schema/outcome validation and receipt-classification code. Its measured conformance records must be explicitly scoped sdk-operation-conformance, must not construct trusted RequestScope, service/Gate handoffs or authoritative receipts, and must never be usable by production authority entry points. A helper-only predicate or direct implementation call that bypasses the shared validation/measurement path is insufficient. Preserve successful Trigger output and all three successful EventHandler lifecycle operations; error-only implementations must fail these positive fixtures. Production typed Guide/Sensor/Trigger/EventHandler paths must finish response and output-schema validation before accepting a receipt; invalid results yield rejected/failed measured outcomes, while valid business-error envelopes retain a separate failed business outcome and never count as positive operation success. Optional side-effecting failures may become skipped only when the external failure outcome is known; structured Unknown and unstructured errors remain Unknown and require observation/recovery. SDK service/Gate rows are exclusively sdk-consumer-negative: reject even internally consistent caller handoffs without issuing a binding, authoritative receipt, or implementation/evaluator call. Envelope, rotation, replay, payload and identity assertions in these rows prove rejection of untrusted candidates, not authentication or durable replay enforcement. The Host-facing ingress contract must be package-neutral and implementable by the separately owned harness-host producer, not an unconditional rejecting stub or a caller-selectable verifier; document the exact release/entrypoint, binding, operation, owner, subject, scope, request/service-payload digest, component/run, policy and evaluator identity handoff. Host-owned verification, configured trust, expiry/rotation and replay enforcement remain in harness-host. The existing downstream dependency harness-host consumes harness-sdk-boundary-evidence and produces harness-host-gate-evidence at artifacts/harness-host/gate-evidence.json; contracts-extension consumes both and emits contracts-extension-final-conformance. Genuine service/Gate acceptance, authenticated handoff transport, accepted-then-replayed rejection across receivers/restart and genuine key rotation are mandatory Host conformance within that artifact, not SDK-local metrics or SDK prerequisites. Mark those downstream obligations not-run in SDK evidence, never passed, and do not add a reverse dependency. This clarification governs all existing test names, counters and historical decision references; no ordinary operation, schema, full identity, provenance, receipt, recovery or replay obligation is removed. The three newly required regression test names are authoring deliverables, not claims of existing passing tests: TestHarnessSDKTypedResponseValidationPrecedesReceiptAcceptance measures malformed response and output-schema violation for both Guide points, both Sensor points, Trigger, and EventHandler execute/observe/cancel (16 rejected results), plus a valid business-error envelope for each of those eight paths without false business success. TestHarnessSDKOptionalUnknownFailureRequiresObservation measures structured outcome_known=false and unstructured errors, retains Unknown without skipped Observation or retry permission, and preserves Required blocking/known Optional failure observations. TestHarnessSDKConformanceEvidenceCannotAuthorizeHostIngress submits actual fixed-runner measurements/request data to the current production service/Gate boundary and proves no authority, bindings, authoritative receipts or implementation/evaluator calls. Keep these child executions in the existing typed-point-describe-contracts, required-optional-failure-policy and service/Gate consumer rows; the fixed selector still has exactly 13 measured semantic rows and seven current-amendment rows. No new row may be faked from test-name presence. Ordinary operation rows carry actual implementation call/result and validator/receipt-classification evidence with full target/operation/provenance identity; service cases are the 15 fixed case IDs checked by the gate. All exact counters derive from those actual parent/child executions, and forbidden-call counters count only calls forbidden for that assertion, not legitimate calls in ordinary positive fixtures. Staged coverage policy, effective only after explicit human acceptance of this amendment: SDK-only raw unfiltered statement coverage must be at least 85%; this does not waive the whole-SDK 90% gate now required of downstream harness-host. Do not filter profiles, change coverage scope, pad the denominator, delete required behavior, manufacture Host proof, or move production code between owners to meet a percentage. The current 79.5% source is not accepted. Add real coverage of ordinary production-used paths and execute the exact reordered commands: broad coverage/vet/race runs first, reset the conformance log, execute every fixed boundary selector, then generate and validate the final 50-test/13-row semantic evidence once. Keep genuine Host conformance not-run in SDK evidence. An ordinary intermediate test, semantic-evidence or raw-coverage failure is implementation feedback, not by itself a terminal blocker: retain the source-bound result, diagnose the specific failing assertion or uncovered production-used path, make a substantive in-contract implementation/test correction, and measure again. Do not submit failing work as successful or advance review/merge/downstream acceptance without every unchanged gate passing. Do not repeat identical attempts without a changed source/test, a distinct evidence-backed diagnostic hypothesis, or a verified infrastructure recovery; existing bounded infrastructure retries, convergence protections and authorized budgets still apply. Request terminal blocking only with specific source-bound evidence that further lawful in-contract work cannot proceed, such as a contract/responsibility/dependency contradiction, missing authorization, indispensable external input, or an independently applicable exhausted control budget. Identify the exact source revision and contract field, actual command/result and retained evidence, attempted substantive corrections, why the next required action is unavailable within the contract, and the precise owner decision or input needed; a below-threshold percentage, one failed attempt or uncertainty about feasibility is insufficient. Use the current work-show-bound blocker protocol for a genuine blocker, never fabricate success or authority. This policy supersedes only the automatic quality-failure stopping interpretation in earlier repair reports, coordinator comments and historical stop clauses; it does not supersede security/design stop conditions or authorize a new architecture, quality relaxation, unlimited retries or a budget reset. After corrections, complete the unchanged source-bound final verification sequence in its existing order, including coverage, vet, race, all fixed selectors, semantic evidence and packaging; diagnostic runs are not final passing evidence. Require the shared immutable measurement-tree redesign described in the objective: preserve recursive per-node authority, public receipt/digest compatibility and complete measured ordinary-operation lineage; four additional regressions are separate from the fixed 50-test/13-row ledger. Their presence never closes a Host-positive obligation.

agent-run-job.description: Rework the thin Job and real production RuntimeDriver vendor as one pinned linux/arm64 package verified from exact shipped bytes.

contract.objective: Deliver the thin AgentRun Job and a production stream-json protocol adapter as a pinned linux/arm64 package: the adapter launches the deployment-configured external runtime executable path and ordered arguments, maps its stdout stream line by line without synthetic native facts, and fail-closes on acceptance/session/terminal protocol violations; no specific third-party runtime binary is bundled.

Do not bundle a specific third-party Runtime binary; launch only the exact external executable path and ordered arguments fixed by deployment-time launch input, without PATH lookup or mutable environment override.

Do not select or reselect Agent, Runtime, model, MCP, Workspace, resource bindings, business routes, or stable lineage.

release-preview.description: Smallest independently PR-able, testable and reviewable delivery boundary for this capability.

contract.objective: Deliver fixed-evidence release readiness and Preview acceptance whose decision idempotency identity is derived from canonical preview input content rather than clock time, whose evidence subject digest exactly equals the current preview input digest, and whose generator records the expected-versus-actual output difference for the same preview input set.
non_goals: Do not include a free clock timestamp in preview Decision identity or idempotency comparison; timestamps are record fields only.
Do not accept substring, member, partial-set, latest-record, or other non-equality evidence binding in place of exact preview input digest equality.
Do not depend on an external regression system; the Preview generator owns the expected-versus-actual difference record for the same normalized input set.

Do not allow reuse of a logical Decision identity under another idempotency key to append or overwrite governed Decision, CommandRecord, AuditEvent, Outbox, or commit indexes; exact replay or deterministic conflict is required.

Do not return PreviewNotReady for a previously approvable submitted subject made stale by changed authoritative preview facts; return the existing StaleSubject/Conflict semantics for both approve and request_changes.
Do not create a ReleaseCandidate, PreviewAcceptance, approval Version, hidden remediation aggregate, or direct WorkUnit/DAG creation path.

source-ownership-baseline-contract.title: Publish immutable source ownership baseline
source-ownership-baseline-contract.description: Root contract that fixes the complete production component owner/source baseline before bootstrap or release tooling executes.

contract.objective: Publish the immutable, exact owner/component/source-path baseline before any component manifest is produced.
non_goals: Do not implement release tooling or produce a release artifact.
Do not infer owners dynamically from a mutable worktree or decomposition manifest at execution time.
verification_commands: mkdir -p artifacts/source-ownership-baseline-contract && python3 -c "import hashlib,json,pathlib,yaml; d=yaml.safe_load(open('contracts/release/source-ownership-baseline.yaml')); assert d['schema']=='omac.source-ownership-baseline/v1'; rows=sorted(d['owners'],key=lambda r:(r['owner_id'],r['component_id'])); assert all(sorted(set(r['source_paths']))==r['source_paths'] and r['source_paths'] and not any(p.startswith('artifacts/') for p in r['source_paths']) for r in rows); assert len(rows)==len({r['owner_id'] for r in rows})==len({r['component_id'] for r in rows})==131; assert sum(len(r['source_paths']) for r in rows)==212; payload=json.dumps(rows,ensure_ascii=False,sort_keys=True,separators=(',',':')).encode(); digest=hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest(); assert digest=='ed452f39d2c7e0e5e7f7b78d0cbf09a37ec2cae872680d0d931c9b4424050872' and d['canonical_sha256']==digest; pathlib.Path('artifacts/source-ownership-baseline-contract/validation.json').write_text(json.dumps({'status':'pass','owner_count':len(rows),'component_count':len({r['component_id'] for r in rows}),'source_path_count':sum(len(r['source_paths']) for r in rows),'canonical_sha256':digest},sort_keys=True))"

contracts-kernel-schema-v1.title: Publish platform-neutral Kernel Contract Schema v1
contracts-kernel-schema-v1.description:
Publish the exact platform-neutral Kernel Contract Schema v1 approved by this amendment. The normative profile is the complete object embedded in the amendment reason and is bound to sha256:568e83d5693ee98a00f5cedf44283e632df9ecb3c4de790aaa19786d9e45b9f5 over its 3314-byte RFC 8785 JCS UTF-8 representation. The implementation must preserve schema_id and exact oac.kernel-contract/v1 version behavior; the twelve fixed limits; all thirteen governed root types; the closed InvocationRequest field set; the seven named evidence/dispatch relations; RFC 8785 JCS UTF-8 canonicalization; SHA-256 lowercase-hex request_digest over the complete closed InvocationRequest with request_digest omitted and all referenced content digests retained in place; recursive unknown-field rejection; unknown-version rejection; duplicate-name rejection; omitted/null distinction; and the independent 65536-byte final canonical request gate. It may write only the final machine-readable schema, its owning OAC Reference document, and the smallest schema validator and seven-case compatibility validator/tests. It must not modify contracts/kernel/**, tune values, make limits configurable, add an approval protocol, or depend on any development-control platform concept.

Canonical profile preimage approved by the amendment (exact JSON object; its RFC 8785 JCS UTF-8 serialization is 3314 bytes and has sha256:568e83d5693ee98a00f5cedf44283e632df9ecb3c4de790aaa19786d9e45b9f5):

  "schema_id": "oac.kernel-contract/v1",
  "kernel_contract_version": {
    "accepted": "oac.kernel-contract/v1",
    "other_versions": "reject"
  },
  "root_types": [
    "InvocationRequest",
    "InputResource",
    "ContractReference",
    "ResponsibilityRequirement",
    "BindingReference",
    "Guide",
    "Conclusion",
    "SubmissionContract",
    "Observation",
    "Decision",
    "WorkSubmission",
    "Question",
    "GateResult"
  ],
  "invocation_request": {
    "closed_object": true,

      "invocation_id",
      "request_digest",
      "workflow_key",
      "work_unit_id",
      "iteration",
      "executor_key",
      "responsibility",
      "objective",
      "contract",
      "guide",
      "submission_contract"
    ],
    "optional_fields": [
      "inputs",
      "prior_conclusions",
      "feedback",
      "allowed_actions"
    ],
    "guide": {
      "closed_object": true,
      "optional_fields": [
        "computational",
        "inferential"
      ]
    }
  },
  "limits": {
    "max_canonical_request_bytes": 65536,
    "max_objective_bytes": 2048,
    "max_display_name_bytes": 128,
    "max_display_description_bytes": 1024,
    "max_inputs": 16,

  },

    "question_submission_persists_as_observation": "A submitted Question is persisted as an immutable Observation before any Answer Decision is admitted.",
    "answer_decision_binds_exact_question_subject": "An Answer Decision binds the exact Question Observation subject identity and digest; latest or unversioned lookup is forbidden.",

contracts-platform-resource-dispatch.title: Validate deterministic dispatch and transition admission closure
contracts-platform-resource-dispatch.description: Rework existing PR #79 at authoring. Own DispatchProjection validation, deterministic dispatch DTO/canonicalization, complete snapshot and creation relation checks, and permanent executable conformance tests in dispatch.go and dispatch_test.go. Retain existing dispatch-owned responsibility and child-link validators without duplicating Plan/Run/Kernel validators. Remove the local-file/process-key authority implementation and caller-value issuance shortcuts; a contract package must not impersonate Platform Core. Reject missing or inconsistent source evidence through a narrow typed read/validation boundary supplied by the application composition root, with production source authentication, fresh reads and atomic consumption owned by platform-workflow-store and Controller semantics owned by workflow-controller. Test-only independent source fixtures prove contract behavior, never live source provenance or production persistence. Revert run.go changes to the integrated Run contract; retain its public wire and opaque private-history boundary. No ownership transfer or acceptance responsibility migration occurs. Preserve all nine blocker identities: BLK-27a9ecc473c9 coherent replay; BLK-30cb5fbecfb2 permanent independent regressions; BLK-8e263e49e120 copy isolation and owner-evidence lookup; BLK-a65075427301 error propagation; BLK-b3496857d6e1 whole-graph binding; BLK-ce8f3c62a3bd single creation relation; BLK-e2630d1188ba Run scope; BLK-ed6c8fd1b773 measured semantic evidence; BLK-f2db8694fa22 restart/rebind. The contract-level portions are verified here. Production portions of source issuance, durable replay and restart remain unclosed until the existing platform-workflow-store implementation proves immutable request history plus CommandRecord/AuditEvent/Outbox commit and CR CAS delivery. The L0 artifact must expose that distinction explicitly to downstream aggregate/Store review rather than report a false end-to-end pass. The second operation strengthens platform-workflow-store-gate with named production tests and source-bound evidence for these production portions; L0 does not consume their future receipts.

contract.objective: Deliver independently executable, fail-closed dispatch contract validation for one complete owner-supplied Workflow/Plan/WorkUnit snapshot, exact inputs and responsibility/Guide, governance evidence, error-returning canonical identities, coherent replay and a single pre-Run creation relation; preserve the integrated Run wire and leave authenticated production issuance, durable transactions and CR writes to their existing implementation owners.
non_goals: Do not change adjacent domain ownership or introduce a competing source of truth.
Do not bypass authorization, admission, CAS, idempotency, review or evidence gates.
Do not preserve unpublished prototype behavior unless the owning design explicitly requires it.

Do not implement a database, local-file authority store, controller loop, process-global MAC issuer, CR writer, or production governance issuer in contracts/workflow/resource. Platform Core is the sole physical writer; Workflow Controller retains semantic ownership. Contract fixtures cannot certify production effects or replace the downstream Store integration gate.

Do not edit run.go, run_test.go, run_external_test.go, plan.go or the integrated public schema/Kernel/Governance/Workspace/Harness contracts. Rebase on the completed Run owner and remove PR-local Run/status wire changes. Dispatch must not call unchecked upstream digest helpers as an authority shortcut; canonicalize its own boundary with explicit errors. If a necessary shared-contract correction cannot be expressed within this boundary, stop for a compensating amendment, never reopen done nodes.

Do not infer trust from caller-supplied matching values, a digest alone, caller-selected allow/admit decisions, public serialization, or a newly constructed matching fixture. Require an owner-source lookup result and explicit revision/freshness binding. An absent, stale, mismatched or unavailable source must fail closed. Production adapter trust and current owner lookup remain application-owned and must not be claimed proven by L0.

Do not introduce a second Plan/Run state machine, duplicate Kernel input assembly/readiness/lifecycle algorithms, alter LifecycleAction identity by including CAS revisions, or migrate acceptance claims/contributions.

Do not collapse canonicalization failures into nil/empty identity values, accept mixed before/after replay snapshots, silently overwrite public mutations from private history during rebind, or reuse stale evidence.

workspace-kubernetes-lifecycle-recovery.title: Implement Kubernetes Workspace lifecycle recovery
workspace-kubernetes-lifecycle-recovery.description: Rework the existing Kubernetes Workspace lifecycle delivery inside its current ownership boundary: make terminal CAS canonical and restart-safe, bind it to the exact recovery record/request/operation/revision and Pod/PVC identity, reject same-kind missing observations for the wrong name or namespace, close public verifier injection with package-owned provider authority, and regenerate synchronized positive/negative evidence without creating another provider or recovery state machine.

contract.objective: Deliver the Kubernetes Pod/PVC lifecycle boundary with credentialed API reads and package-owned, unforgeable provider/CNI proof bound to exact authority/provider identity, version, digest, credential provenance, object kind/namespace/name/UID/resourceVersion, request/operation lineage, complete NetworkPolicy selector/effective-rule semantics, and a provider/store-created canonical serializable terminal receipt authenticated by that authority and returned by the actual conditional write, bound to the loaded recovery record, exact Pod/PVC/NetworkPolicy observation, expected and committed revision, and included in the outer proof digest; validate every candidate and restart-rehydrated receipt before mutation, preserve prior records on failed writes, enforce immutable store ownership and terminal delete preconditions, fail closed on same-UID resourceVersion drift, and provide deterministic concurrent-release stale-loser semantics while retaining Unknown/Lost whenever any exact proof or identity binding is unavailable.
non_goals: Do not change adjacent domain ownership, add a second Workspace runtime/provider, create a competing recovery state machine, or move final provider registration out of the existing Workspace aggregate.

Do not accept caller-supplied readiness, provider identity, object metadata, NetworkPolicy enforcement, terminal evidence, an externally implementable or injected verifier, mutable labels/annotations, or process-local witness pointers as authority; any in-process witness may only be a derived cache of validated durable provider proof.

Do not advertise NetworkPolicyEnforcement, StrongIsolation, or another runtime capability unless the credentialed package-owned provider boundary returns an unforgeable canonical attestation that validates against the exact fetched objects and complete effective selector/rule semantics.

Do not allow invalid or non-matching MatchLabels/MatchExpressions, wrong-kind evidence, same-kind missing observations with a wrong name or namespace, malformed request/operation identity, cross-namespace Pod/PVC pairing, terminal proof replay across records or operations, revision drift, or invalid/unconditional terminal evidence to satisfy lifecycle or cleanup conditions; memory and test stores must use the same conditional-write boundary.

Do not delete the last recovery descriptor before ordered Pod-before-PVC cleanup and both provider-owned terminal CAS proofs are durably rehydrated and validated against the loaded recovery record; do not turn timeout, restart, missing proof, Unknown, or Lost into invented Released, Failed, or success.

Do not implement source materialization, descriptor-relative filesystem mutation, or downstream production-conformance ownership in this node. Deterministic credentialed client-go/provider fixtures must exercise the production boundary but must not be represented as a live CNI deployment result.

Do not treat a public-field self-hash, arbitrary StoreIdentity, locally derived expectedRevision+1 value, caller-shaped receipt, or mutable process-local token as provider/store authenticity or as evidence of the actual conditional-write result; the outer canonical proof must not exclude the authenticated receipt.

Do not mutate a shared terminal map or persisted RecoveryRecord before complete candidate validation, permit a rejected second-kind write to alter the prior record, let SaveIfRevision rebind immutable Ownership, or let DeleteIfRevision bypass valid paired terminal/release preconditions.

Do not leave concurrent release behavior scheduler-dependent or require only one lucky package run; define the stale-loser result including the post-delete case and prove it repeatedly under GOMAXPROCS=1.

contracts-kernel-executor-resolution-evi.title: Publish responsibility-bound executor-resolution evidence contracts
contracts-kernel-executor-resolution-evi.description: Compensating versioned public-contract producer on the original issue/PR. Consume the reviewed additive catalog first; keep frozen v1 sources and residual tests intact, implement new closed contextual behavior only in contracts/kernel/lifecyclev1, and pass the real unchanged frozen-v1 consumer before publication. Downstream adapter/lifecycle responsibilities are unchanged.

contract.objective: Publish the complete closed, versioned lifecycle/executor-resolution contract in the additive contracts/kernel/lifecyclev1 package, preserving the exact published contracts/kernel/contracts.go and validation.go bytes and all governed oac.kernel-contract/v1 wire semantics. Import, do not redefine, frozen InvocationRequest and governed roots. Where new lifecycle, Gate, Run or Selection fields/requiredness cannot be represented by frozen types, expose explicit versioned extension DTOs/envelopes and contextual validators, not changed legacy types or a permissive fallback. Restore PR77 residual review_regression_test.go to the unchanged main baseline. All extension entry points, recursive schema parity, canonical retained Decisions and request-bound active Run admission must fail closed, and the unchanged downstream frozen-v1 resource consumer must pass on the exact publication head. Publish one ownership-accounted component with regenerated same-head evidence. Required executable cases: DispatchExecution and StartReview each reject missing SelectionEvidence and validate it against authoritative Workflow/Plan/PlanNode/WorkUnit/iteration/subject/responsibility, current capability snapshot, exact persisted MissingExecutor fact, immutable InvocationRequest and applicable active Run. Replace the former positive missing-evidence branch; include absent and foreign/stale evidence negatives for both action kinds. Active Run binding requires both non-empty InvocationID and RequestDigest, compared unconditionally to the current request; test neither present, each missing separately, and mismatched identity. Explicit pre-Run context remains valid only before a Run exists. LifecycleEvidenceRecord contextual admission validates the complete persisted typed selection Decision and its canonical DecisionID/Digest, subject/outcome, typed payload and exact persistence before authorizing it. Test independently forged non-empty ID and digest on an otherwise valid persisted typed Decision. The versioned Gate evaluator binding validates both content and configuration digests at Harness/Plan authoring, not only GateResult storage. Test missing configuration at both authoring and persisted gate boundaries. Recursive spec parity must execute Go-backed fixtures for every nested property/type/tag/requiredness, closed enum, canonical identity relation, full action compatibility branch, iteration matrix and lifecycle fixture. Mutation tests alter each dimension while keeping top-level markers/field names and must be rejected. Do not treat field-set or closed_objects assertions as semantic evidence. Keep permanent regressions for the five previously fixed blockers: every Action digest, persisted wrapper validation, exact WorkUnit contract identity, Gate iteration limits, and no Platform resource source changes. Unknown fields, duplicate members, explicit nulls, foreign history, ambiguous responsibilities and stale iterations remain fail-closed. Amendment AITEAM-1002: close the rejected PR82 head's remaining semantic defects on the same owner/issue/PR. At GateEvaluatorSet.ValidateAgainst authoring admission, an omitted active Harness allowed_outcomes means exactly the fixed Kernel set {Pass, AwaitDecision, Rework, Reject, Error}; compare complete effective sets, not subset containment or a conditional comparison. An omitted-list Harness and a versioned Pass-only policy must fail; the complete fixed set must pass. Explicit active Harness lists require exact set equality too. Reject unknown/duplicate outcomes; preserve content/configuration digest and binding identity checks. For recursive extension-spec validation, use the exact declared fields of each individual object, never a generic metadata superset: identity/storage_key are legal only at schema nodes that explicitly declare them. Preserve legitimate declared metadata. Add the five permanent named subtests below to the existing twelve-test suite; each must start from a valid control fixture, mutate only its named dimension, call the real exported contextual/parity validator and fail if the mutation is accepted. No test-only validator or hard-coded evidence. Keep the already fixed persisted RunSummary/absent ActiveRun negatives for both action kinds and the transition required_fact, terminal target_rules, and Gate Reject/Error target/iteration mutations. Regenerate the seven declared artifacts from the corrected publication head after all gates pass. This is typed contract/conformance evidence, not proof of Host persistence or production effects. Required permanent subtests: TestExtensionSpecRecursiveSemanticParity/missing_executor_wire_identity, TestExtensionSpecRecursiveSemanticParity/transition_closed_payload_identity, TestExtensionSpecRecursiveSemanticParity/parameter_type_storage_key, TestExtensionSpecRecursiveSemanticParity/runtime_selection_storage_key, TestHarnessDefinitionRejectsIncompleteGateEvaluatorConfiguration/omitted_harness_effective_outcomes. Each subtest emits exactly one OMAC_SEMANTIC_CASE= JSON object via t.Log with fields case (its full test name) and accepted (the actual exported validator error == nil boolean). Emission must happen after the real call even if accepted=true; assert rejection separately. The metric verifier consumes Go test JSON output plus pass/run/skip/fail records, never self-authored JSON constants. Existing parity mutations remain mandatory; spec_semantic_mutation_accept_count covers every parity negative in the suite and must be derived from actual calls, with the four listed nested cases a mandatory subset. Emit the same marker for all parity negative subtests, and ensure each marker has a matching executed non-skipped passing test. The Gate case is counted separately.
non_goals: Do not modify source outside the original nine owned roots plus contracts/kernel/lifecyclev1/** registered by kernel-lifecycle-additive-ownership. Preserve frozen contracts.go and validation.go bytes exactly; reverting the existing out-of-scope PR77 residual test delta is cleanup only, not an ownership grant.
Do not implement Host persistence or lifecycle reduction in this node.
Do not change the frozen oac.kernel-contract/v1 InvocationRequest field set, limits, canonicalization, digest, or unknown-version behavior.
Do not accept a fact as historical solely because its iteration differs or use an untagged required-review fallback as responsibility identity.
Do not rewrite or reopen completed contracts-kernel-public or contracts-kernel-schema-v1 runtime facts.
Do not change contracts/workflow/resource/** or its published hashes to make this gate green; downstream adapter remains its existing owner and depends on this verified component.

Do not rewrite kernel-contract-v1.json, the frozen schema reference, source_release, canonical profile or the published source hash constants in either compatibility verifier. Add extension validation without replacing the frozen validation path.

Do not run v1 permissive validation as authorization for a versioned lifecycle execution; the extension dispatcher and its downstream adapters must invoke the mandatory contextual extension admission.

Do not claim production persistence or Host enforcement from fixture state: this component proves typed wire/context validation only. B-class production responsibility remains with its existing effect owners.

agentrun-cancellation-prerequisite.title: Resolve the retained AgentRun cancellation prerequisite with owner diagnosis and verified remedy
agentrun-cancellation-prerequisite.description: New compensating authoring node for the exact AITEAM-820 cancellation reject, owned by the Runtime prerequisite Agent. Diagnose before changing source; deliver either the minimal proven source/fixture repair or a demonstrated bounded environment remedy in a separate PR. No Audit edits, completed-owner reopen or acceptance migration. See the source-bound contract for stop conditions and reproducible closure.

contract.objective: Resolve the AgentRun cancellation prerequisite through independently reproduced source-bound causal/remedy evidence for the cancellation/Wait failure class, under the separately human-approved historical-evidence replacement decision H; retain the original AITEAM-820 failure as causally unclassified history. Preserve already-approved S and independently prove its held-original-Wait, deadlines, diagnostic and teardown obligations before normal merge and Audit re-verification.
non_goals: Do not ship AGENTRUN_FIXTURE_MODE, fixture marker/PID hooks, blockForever, synthetic all-event generation, or any other test-selected behavior in cmd/agentrun-job/vendor, driver production code, or the release bundle; malformed-stream fixtures belong only in testdata or non-release test packages.

Do not bundle a specific third-party Runtime binary; launch only the exact external executable path and ordered arguments fixed by deployment-time launch input, without PATH lookup or mutable environment override.

Do not accept duplicate started/resumed records, any non-empty line after terminal, an acceptance kind that mismatches new versus resume mode, or an ordinary event carrying a foreign vendor session identity.
Do not complete successfully until the terminal record, clean vendor EOF, child exit, critical-tail persistence, and package-proven event provenance are all validated.
Do not select or reselect Agent, Runtime, model, MCP, Workspace, resource bindings, business routes, or stable lineage.
Do not require changes to merged scripts/release tooling; package construction, source scanning, protocol verification and exact-byte checks remain under cmd/agentrun-job/**.

Do not modify PR #78, Audit/Usage or its permitted AgentDefinition/Preview consumer changes, canonical schemas, other domain behavior, the live DAG, completed-node contracts, source ownership catalogs, or retry/coverage/security thresholds.

Do not treat unchanged-tree green runs, a possible ordering race, observer improvements, S approval or approval of H as an implementation pass or reconstruction of the original AITEAM-820 ten-second failure. Retain every failed attempt. After H is explicitly approved, independently proven prospective causal/remedy evidence under the cause-and-remedy gate may satisfy this prerequisite without claiming the original process state or historical cause was established. If that replacement evidence cannot be established, submit a precise owner-decision blocker and leave the prerequisite unresolved.

Do not skip, quarantine, delete, soften or increase the ten-second process-disappearance deadline of the failing test to obtain a pass. Preserve cancellation reaching the actual vendor, child exit AND reaping, one Execute/stream, bounded drain/backpressure, critical-tail ACK ordering and no CompleteAgentRun after persistent append failure. If observation/fixture code is wrong, prove the defect and preserve or strengthen those assertions with positive and negative controls, including detection of a genuinely live unreaped child; do not redefine a zombie as reaped.

Do not decide source versus environment from kill -0 alone. Bind observations to the actual child identity, parent/wait ownership and process state, accounting for PID reuse, zombies and permission/probe errors. Explain cancellation-to-exit-to-Wait ordering using the existing runner, SDK and driver call paths; instrumentation belongs only in tests or bounded redacted evidence, not production fixture hooks.

Supporting production/test edits outside cmd/agentrun-job are permitted only in the existing internal/agentrun or runtime-sdk cancellation/session-close path when causally required by the source-bound cancellation/Wait failure class and approved S obligations, not on an invented historical causal link. This does not transfer the completed SDK or Job owners or authorize SDK product imports, unrelated MCP/planning repair or broader refactoring. Sole additional supporting-file exception: this compensation node may remove exactly the redundant indirect gopkg.in/yaml.v3 v3.0.1 requirement from root go.mod, retaining the existing direct requirement at v3.0.1 and every other byte; go.sum must remain byte-identical. This is a one-defect implementation authorization, not transfer of the canonical bootstrap-go package/source-catalog ownership. The only additional supporting-document authorization is to align docs/design/detailed/06-agent-runtime-detailed-design.md sections 8 and 8.2 and docs/references/execution/agent-runtime.md sections 7 and 9 with already-approved S: confirmed owning Wait plus expired cancellation channel-close deadline permits the existing unknown/no-completion failure even if driver Events/Result remain open; pending Wait still retains its original owner. Preserve normal success EOF/terminal/critical-tail ACK ordering. No other design, governance, schema, catalog or completed-owner edits are authorized. This narrow documentation responsibility is explicit in the ownership migration; it is not a new runtime policy.

A source/fixture cause requires a permanent failing-before/passing-after regression and the minimal correction in a new owner PR based on main. An environment-only cause requires independently reproducible before/after process evidence and a durable bounded environment/setup/cleanup recipe committed with the owner PR; no privilege expansion, global process killing, host/cluster policy change or new deployment requirement is authorized. If such a tradeoff is genuinely necessary, stop for an explicit decision.

The diagnostic deliverable must pin the original rejected HEAD and report/ledger hashes, actual tested source SHA/tree, Go version, OS/architecture, relevant process/reaper conditions, commands/exit codes and redacted evidence digests. Distinguish proven source/fixture or environment cause from unproven hypotheses. Describe the concrete remedy and how Audit reproduces it after merge; package source and release evidence must name the actual new PR HEAD, never the rejected HEAD or a temporary modified tree. Separate original retained observation, reproduced prospective cause/remedy, and approved residual uncertainty in diagnosis.md. A prospective source/fixture or bounded environment proof is not retroactive proof of the original failure; do not assert that the original failure is repaired or its environment cause excluded.

Preserve the inherited agent-run-job release/coverage/protocol gates as written below, including the pinned linux/arm64 shipped pair and exact-byte package verification. Native reproducer results and shipped-package results are distinct evidence. Do not claim the old merged package proves a changed implementation.

NEW HUMAN DECISION H IS REQUIRED BEFORE APPLY OR IMPLEMENTATION: explicitly approve replacing proof of the original AITEAM-820 historical cause/remedy with the evidence-bound prospective cause/remedy gate below, while recording the original cause as unknown and accepting that recurrence from an unobserved historical environment/identity/reaping cause is not excluded. Without H approval preserve the unresolved blocker/work and do not apply or dispatch. Alternatively retain the original contract and supply authoritative original process/Wait records if recovered; no new live-environment access is authorized.

Under explicitly approved option S, replace the contradictory unconditional finite-cleanup-plus-Wait-before-return requirement with bounded software shutdown and an explicit pending-Wait retention exception. Cancellation still reaches the exact configured Runtime through the existing Job -> linked stream-json adapter -> Runtime chain. Keep the adapter's five-second TERM grace then group/direct SIGKILL, and the existing ten-second driver observation windows; deadline expiry is not proof of death/reaping. Retain the single parent owning each child Wait. Do not SIGKILL the adapter merely because its outer grace expired while its Runtime Wait is unconfirmed: that destroys the inner wait owner and cannot prove Runtime reaping. The adapter must not exit, and Job Run/Execute-start failure must not return, until the Runtime owning Wait followed by the adapter owning Wait are established. Apply the same rule to startup/acceptance failure, malformed stream, timeout, append failure and ordinary cancellation. Never return from startFailure after a failed bounded killAndWait as if ownership had been discharged.

The pending-Wait exception is not permission for avoidable software deadlock. Decouple cancellation escalation and the single owning Wait from blocked acceptance/stdin writes, stdout Scan/forwarding, stderr-copy EOF and public event/result consumers in the existing driver/adapter cancellation path. Close owned pipe endpoints on cancellation/failure and bound post-exit I/O joins; treat forced pipe closure as incomplete evidence, never clean success. A pinned Go Cmd.WaitDelay can bound post-exit copying, but cannot replace Process.Wait, reap a live process, bound a kernel wait that never returns, or by itself unblock caller-owned Scanner/Write calls before Wait. Preserve clean EOF and terminal validation on success. After verified owning Wait, permanently open driver channels must yield the existing unknown/no-completion failure at the existing cancellation close deadline (20 seconds from cancellation, immediate if already expired), rather than continue waiting for channel EOF. The runner's 30-second drain window must not conceal an avoidable post-Wait wait; only the explicitly identified pending owning-Wait barrier may remain outstanding. Do not add a supervisor, daemon, sidecar, SDK product import, new protocol/package/status schema, privileges, host/cluster policy or deployment prerequisite.

Pending Wait is an unknown physical cleanup condition, not succeeded, cancelled, failed-with-proven-exit, or reaped. At the expired cleanup window expose one bounded redacted diagnostic through the existing Job diagnostic path; do not claim that stderr/logs are a persisted business Observation or that an unavailable Platform API accepted it. Never call CompleteAgentRun after persistent append failure or manufacture a SDK terminal to unlock the runner. Memory and buffers remain bounded, without a busy loop or unbounded diagnostic/event accumulation. While the owner remains alive, it continues its original Wait and does not start another Runtime/Execute. If that owner or node dies, in-memory wait ownership is lost: do not assert reaping, same-Run resume, safe retry or successful cleanup from the restart/Pod state. Preserve Unknown and the existing observe-before-retry/new-AgentRun boundary; no controller, observer, reaper-adoption or credential-revocation capability is created by this amendment. Retained processes can continue occupying resources and may retain access until exit/lease expiry; user approval of S must acknowledge this availability and residual-access risk, not treat nonterminal waiting as complete containment.

integration_gates.name: harness-sdk-gate
integration_gates.delivery_goal: Deliver the complete protocol-neutral public harness.oac.dev/v1 SDK boundary with typed Describe, execute, observe, cancel, result, and error unions; preserve exact Package/entrypoint, Extension/binding, operation, owner, subject, scope, request digest, and service payload digest through every public binding path. Remove every public authority constructor that lets a caller choose both Host signing and trust verification inputs, and expose only the package-neutral consumer/verification side of opaque service and Gate handoffs. The SDK must define a usable Host-facing ingress contract without implementing the Host producer: arbitrary callers and ExtensionPackages must be unable to mint an authoritative RequestScope, GateEvaluatorBinding, receipt, or evaluator invocation. Replace the obsolete missing-symbol regression with a structurally valid attempt against the current public API and prove zero binding, receipt, and evaluator calls. Remove all SDK-owned or same-package test-only Host authority bridges. Every SDK-local fixture must emit source-revision-bound measured evidence for its exact scoped assertion; the Gate consumer row may pass only by proving the negative boundary, must report registered_gate_positive_path_count=0 and authoritative_gate_positive_claim_count=0, and must identify its scope as sdk-boundary rather than representing full Host-backed Gate conformance. Produce harness-sdk-boundary-evidence for the downstream harness-host producer. Preserve typed operation-schema validation, successful Trigger/EventHandler, bounded offline schema resolution, Required/Optional behavior, Unknown recovery, safe retry/cancel, coverage, race, vet, and deterministic sdk/harness packaging. The mandatory genuine Host-installed positive path and final combined semantic verdict remain downstream responsibilities of harness-host and contracts-extension. SDK-local positive operation conformance is not Host authorization: the fixed SDK conformance runner may execute ordinary typed Describe/Guide/Sensor/Executor/Trigger/EventHandler implementations with deterministic, non-authoritative request data and the same production input/response/schema/outcome validation and receipt-classification code. Its measured conformance records must be explicitly scoped sdk-operation-conformance, must not construct trusted RequestScope, service/Gate handoffs or authoritative receipts, and must never be usable by production authority entry points. A helper-only predicate or direct implementation call that bypasses the shared validation/measurement path is insufficient. Preserve successful Trigger output and all three successful EventHandler lifecycle operations; error-only implementations must fail these positive fixtures. Production typed Guide/Sensor/Trigger/EventHandler paths must finish response and output-schema validation before accepting a receipt; invalid results yield rejected/failed measured outcomes, while valid business-error envelopes retain a separate failed business outcome and never count as positive operation success. Optional side-effecting failures may become skipped only when the external failure outcome is known; structured Unknown and unstructured errors remain Unknown and require observation/recovery. SDK service/Gate rows are exclusively sdk-consumer-negative: reject even internally consistent caller handoffs without issuing a binding, authoritative receipt, or implementation/evaluator call. Envelope, rotation, replay, payload and identity assertions in these rows prove rejection of untrusted candidates, not authentication or durable replay enforcement. The Host-facing ingress contract must be package-neutral and implementable by the separately owned harness-host producer, not an unconditional rejecting stub or a caller-selectable verifier; document the exact release/entrypoint, binding, operation, owner, subject, scope, request/service-payload digest, component/run, policy and evaluator identity handoff. Host-owned verification, configured trust, expiry/rotation and replay enforcement remain in harness-host. The existing downstream dependency harness-host consumes harness-sdk-boundary-evidence and produces harness-host-gate-evidence at artifacts/harness-host/gate-evidence.json; contracts-extension consumes both and emits contracts-extension-final-conformance. Genuine service/Gate acceptance, authenticated handoff transport, accepted-then-replayed rejection across receivers/restart and genuine key rotation are mandatory Host conformance within that artifact, not SDK-local metrics or SDK prerequisites. Mark those downstream obligations not-run in SDK evidence, never passed, and do not add a reverse dependency. This clarification governs all existing test names, counters and historical decision references; no ordinary operation, schema, full identity, provenance, receipt, recovery or replay obligation is removed. The three newly required regression test names are authoring deliverables, not claims of existing passing tests: TestHarnessSDKTypedResponseValidationPrecedesReceiptAcceptance measures malformed response and output-schema violation for both Guide points, both Sensor points, Trigger, and EventHandler execute/observe/cancel (16 rejected results), plus a valid business-error envelope for each of those eight paths without false business success. TestHarnessSDKOptionalUnknownFailureRequiresObservation measures structured outcome_known=false and unstructured errors, retains Unknown without skipped Observation or retry permission, and preserves Required blocking/known Optional failure observations. TestHarnessSDKConformanceEvidenceCannotAuthorizeHostIngress submits actual fixed-runner measurements/request data to the current production service/Gate boundary and proves no authority, bindings, authoritative receipts or implementation/evaluator calls. Keep these child executions in the existing typed-point-describe-contracts, required-optional-failure-policy and service/Gate consumer rows; the fixed selector still has exactly 13 measured semantic rows and seven current-amendment rows. Under the selected current schema, old WorkflowParameters/SystemEnvironment/PolicyEnvironment wrapper-presence is not reinstated; required configuration content is represented by the exact ConfigurationDigest and individually supplied typed values.
